As a complimentary term it formed the Roman proper name Constantius, and numerous other male names, especially among royalty. "Two things," he says, "threaten us with utter anarchy—the aggression of the Sinn Feiners and the weakness of the authorities. Those whose duty is to govern are giving way all along the line. Munsey, owner of the New York Sun and the Evening Sun who recently bought the New York Herald and Evening Telegram from the estate of the late James Gordon Bennett, announced tonight that the Sun and the Herald would be amalgamated February 1, under the name of the Sun and the New York Herald.

Mr. Munsey added that it had been his wish to preserve the Herald as an independent entity, but this could not be done as it would have been in opposition to all the laws of economies; all the laws of sound business.

"The Herald printing plant is archaic and worn to the breaking point," he said, adding "that new equipment could not be installed under a year and 6 months and then it would cost million dollars or more."

"The Sun does not need the Herald in combination, but the Herald needs the Sun," Mr. Munsey said. "It will get from the Sun the vigor and energy and initiative that the Herald has lacked in recent years. It will get too, as great measure of prestige as it gives."

Mr. Munsey said that his plans as to the Evening Telegram and the Evening Sun had not been completed.
